full_judgment: On 23.12.1953 a requisition under section 5 of the Public Demands Recovery Act was sent to the Certificate Officer, Chittagong for realisation of Agricultural Income-Tax by the Agricultural Income-Tax Officer. Subsequently there were other requisitions on similar grounds. Consequently certificate cases being Certificate case Nos. 107 G (CML) and 108 G(CML) of 1953-54 and 99 G (Agri-Tax) of 1959-60 were started. These cases were lumped together and analogously dealt with. Ultimately a certificate sale took place on 1.4.1961 in respect of the properties belonging to the petitioners predecessors and the plaintiffs and others auction purchased the same. The sale was confirmed on 3.6.1961. The auction purchasers claimed that they took possession on 8.8.1961. The petitioners and their mother alleged that they came to know of the sale for the first time on 21.11.1962 when some auction purchasers asked them to vacate the house at Cox's Bazar. Thereafter the petitioners and their mother filed an application on 10.1.1963 for setting aside the sale under section 23 of the Public Demands Recovery Act. The Certificate Officer held that the petition under section 23 of the Public Demands Recovery Act was time barred. He, therefore, rejected the petition. As against the said order of rejection the petitioners and their mother (since dead) filed appeal before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong. The Additional Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong found that a case was made out for extending the period of limitation. He, therefore, set aside the auction sale. Thereupon all the auction purchasers filed a revision before the Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong which was dismissed by the Additional Commissioner, Chittagong on 1.5.1967. The auction purchasers filed a revision before the Board of Revenue, East Pakistan which was dismissed on 18.8.1968. Thereafter, one of the auction purchasers named Kabir Ahmed filed Writ Petition No. 435 of 1967 in the High Court of the then East Pakistan challenging the aforesaid orders of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Chittagong, Additional Commissioner, Chittagong Division and Member, Board of Revenue, East Pakistan. The Writ Petition was discharged on 3.6.1971 by Mr. Justice Maksum-ul-Hakim and Mr. Justice Badrul Haider Chowdhury. Therefore, the said Kabir Ahmed filed application for leave to appeal before the Appellate Division Supreme Court. But the leave was refused. Thereafter the present plaintiffs who were not parties to the Writ Petition have filed the instant suits. The defendants, the judgment debtors in the certificate case, made application before the Court concerned for rejection of the plaints on the ground that the suit was barred by res judicata and law generally.
